newsitem.title: USA: Quidel says settlement may cause expense.
newsitem.headline: Quidel says settlement may cause expense.

text.p: Quidel Corp said Tuesday it has settled the lawsuit filed in April 1997 by Becton Dickinson and Co, and estimates the terms of the settlement could result in an annual expense of about $1.9 million.
The lawsuit alleged Quidel's strep and chlamydia products and certain of its pregnancy and ovulation products infringe two Becton patents.

Quidel said under the settlement agreement, it received a license from Becton under both patents in exchange for a cash license fee, and agreed to pay a royalty on net sales of the products beginning April 1.
Quidel said it also provided Becton a license to the its Q-Label technology with a royalty payable on future sales.
Quidel said it estimates the annual amortization of the license fee and the royalty payments, based on current product sales, could result in an annual expense of $1.9 million.
Quidel said it believes it has opportunities to mitigate the impact of this additional expense through sales growth and improved margins from favorable product mix.
